summary: Kathleen Kenyon (1906–1978) was a scholar in history and archaeology. She studied at St Paul's Girls' School (~1918–1925) and Somerville College (~1925–1928), later holding posts at the University of London, UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) specialized in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University as Associate Professor of Religion (~1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald (born 1952) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Thubten Yeshe (~1974–1984), Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned degrees from Juniata College and the University of Michigan (PhD under Walter M. Spink, and MD), completed residency at University of Utah Hospital, and holds a fellowship at the University of Utah (2024–2026).
Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 1998) and the University of Manitoba (attested 1999).

Katia Buffetrille (born 1948) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her degrees including a PhD at Paris Nanterre University, studying under Alexander W. Macdonald, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale.

Katia Chirkova works in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. She studied at Beijing Language and Culture University and Leiden University (PhD), holding posts at Leiden University (2003–2005), the International Institute for Asian Studies (2005–2006), and the Centre de Recherches Linguistiques sur l'Asie Orientale (2006).

Katja Triplett (born 1965) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Marburg and held posts at SOAS, University of Marburg, University of Göttingen, Lichtenberg-Kolleg, University of Leipzig, and Leibniz University Hannover.

Katragadda Paddayya (born 1943) is an archaeologist and Indologist. He completed his doctoral degree at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–1968) and served as a professor, including Professor of Geo-archaeology, at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1972–2008).

Katrin Querl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Munich, Kagyu College, and the University of Vienna (Dr. phil.), holding posts at the University of Leipzig and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and served at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (1986, 1988–2003).
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1964–1968) and served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1999).

Katsuji Fujioka (1872–1935) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905). He succeeded Kazutoshi Ueda in 1910 and served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo (1910–1933).
Katsumi Kuroita (1874–1946) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held a post there from approximately 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and in Paris under Gadjin Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Hisashi Sato, serving as a professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010) and joining the Japan Academy in 2006.

Katsumi Okimoto (1943–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1973) and served as a professor, director, and professor emeritus at Hanazono University (~1985–2014).

Katsumi Tanabe (born 1941) specializes in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1968) and held academic posts at Kanazawa University (~1993–1999) and Chuo University (~1999–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Kyoto University, holding posts there (1933–1943), at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Nara National Museum (1949–1967), Kansai University, and Ryukoku University (~1964–1980).

Kavita Singh (1964–2023) worked in archaeology and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MS University of Baroda, and Panjab University, and held posts including dean at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2001), College of Art, Delhi, and National Institute of Technology Delhi.
